title: The Inventory of Everything That Exists: the Sailor, the Number 01662, and the Cape for Judgment Day
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Sergipe: the Farm and the Apprentice

stops.name: Japaratuba, birth under two dates
stops.date_confidence: contradictory: English Wikipedia gives 14 May 1909 with 16 March 1911 as an alternate, Portuguese Wikipedia gives 16 March 1911, the museum's own biography gives 1909 without a month; the conflict is not resolved and the earlier value used here expresses no preference. An earlier research pass carried a third date, 10 May 1911, which appears in no source and is struck.
stops.campa: In the sugar country of Sergipe a son is born to Adriano Bispo do Rosário and Blandina Francisca de Jesus. The registers that should fix the day do not agree, and the disagreement outlives everyone who could settle it: one encyclopedia gives a May day in 1909, another a March day in 1911, the museum that now carries his name gives 1909 and no month at all. He will spend fifty years counted by an institution as patient 01662. The first number attached to him, the year of his own birth, is not counted right.
suggested_refs: The civil and parish registers of Japaratuba, Sergipe, which no reachable source cites for either candidate birth date

stops.name: Rural Japaratuba, raised by cacau farmers
stops.date_confidence: undated: sources state the fostering without naming the couple, the farm, or the years involved; 1915 is a placeholder inside his childhood and carries no evidential weight
stops.campa: A couple who farm cacau take the boy in and raise him. No source names them, names their land, or says what changed in his own family to put him there; the record keeps the arrangement and loses everyone inside it. He works the ground as a child in a state whose wealth is sugar and whose labor is Black, one generation after abolition. Nothing dates the day he leaves. Between this farm and the naval school at Aracaju no document places him anywhere, and the missing years are his first fifteen.
suggested_refs: The unnamed cacau-farming household of the Japaratuba region, unlocated in any accessible source

stops.name: Aracaju, the Escola de Aprendizes de Marinheiros
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month by Portuguese Wikipedia; the school's building within period Aracaju was not established in this pass and the coordinate is the city center, an approximation
stops.campa: In February he enters the naval apprentices' school at Aracaju, the first institution to number him, uniform him, and tell him where to stand. The Sergipe coast gives way to drill and rank and a written chain of command. He is a boy off a cacau farm learning the grammar of an ordered world: kit laid out the same way each morning, every man in his place, every place recorded. Half a century later, inside another institution that numbers and uniforms and orders him, he will inventory the whole of creation and stitch each thing its label.
suggested_refs: The Escola de Aprendizes de Marinheiros de Sergipe, Aracaju, and its 1925 enrollment books

stops.name: Ilha das Cobras, enlistment in the Navy of War
stops.date_confidence: attested; Portuguese Wikipedia splits the year into the February school and the December enlistment for a nine-year term, English Wikipedia gives only 1925
stops.campa: In December he signs for nine years in the Marinha de Guerra and is based on Guanabara Bay, under the hill forts and the cranes of the naval arsenal. Rio takes him in as it takes every recruit off the northeast coast, by ship and by paperwork. Not one vessel he served aboard is named in any record reached here; the nine years are attested and their itinerary is not. What survives of the sea in him is the thing he builds by hand decades later, model ships and rigged veleiros made of asylum waste, sailing nowhere out of Jacarepaguá.
suggested_refs: Marinha de Guerra service records for the 1925-1933 term, not located in any reachable archive

stops.name: Montevideo, a port in the retellings
stops.date_confidence: tradition, unverified: secondary accounts place his ship at River Plate ports on routine patrols and goodwill cruises, no log or muster roll confirming the call was located in this pass, and the year is a placeholder inside the service span
stops.campa: The telling of his life carries him south to the Puerto de Montevideo, one of the River Plate calls the Brazilian navy made on patrol and on show. No log names him at this quay. The claim repeats itself from retelling to retelling without ever touching a document, the way a rumor hardens into a biography. He is placed here by tradition alone, and the quay is entered as tradition, because leaving it out would tidy the life and putting it in unmarked would forge one.
suggested_refs: Brazilian naval cruise logs of the River Plate stations, 1926-1933, unconsulted and possibly extant
sources: Traditional secondary biographical accounts of Bispo's naval service, flagged unconfirmed

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the second unverified quay
stops.date_confidence: tradition, unverified, on exactly the footing of the Montevideo call; the atlas's canonical Buenos Aires anchor at -34.6037, -58.3816 is deliberately not used, since the interlock lens returned an explicit negative finding that Bispo's itinerary does not touch it
stops.campa: Buenos Aires stands beside Montevideo in the same accounts and rests on the same nothing. A ship is said to have reached it; the ship is not named, the date is not given, the source is a retelling of a retelling. The atlas keeps a canonical pin for this city, load-bearing under half a dozen other lives. It is not used here. This mark is a dockside guess attached to a story, set apart from the anchor on purpose, so that the guess can never be mistaken for a crossing that never happened.
suggested_refs: Port of Buenos Aires arrival records for Brazilian naval vessels, 1926-1933, unconsulted
sources: Traditional secondary biographical accounts of Bispo's naval service, flagged unconfirmed
Interlock finding: canonical Buenos Aires pin explicitly not inheritable for this subject

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the boxer in two weights
stops.date_confidence: attested from 1928 onward by Portuguese Wikipedia, with no closing date given; individual match venues are not specified in any source consulted, and national competition is reported rather than documented
stops.campa: He boxes for the Navy, lightweight and then middleweight, and by some accounts fights nationally. In the ring he is not a recruit but a name printed in results, a body trained to be looked at while it works. This is the only stretch of his life in which the public attention on him is of his own making. Every later showing of him is arranged by somebody else: a magazine photographer inside the ward, a critic at the gate, a museum with his name across the door and his patient number in the file.
suggested_refs: Brazilian navy boxing championship results, 1928-1933, unlocated

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, discharged for indiscipline
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by Portuguese Wikipedia; the infractions themselves are not itemized in any source consulted
stops.campa: In the eighth year of a nine-year term the Marinha de Guerra puts him out for accumulated infractions. The sources give the verdict and withhold the charges. He walks into civilian Rio without rank, without kit, without the timetable that had told him where to be since he was a boy at Aracaju. The city receiving him is the capital of a republic three years into Vargas, and it has work for a strong man with a boxer's shoulders and no papers of any other kind.
suggested_refs: The discharge file of the 1933 expulsion, unlocated

segments.name: The Light Company and the Lawyer's House

stops.name: Light e Power depot, washing the trams
stops.date_confidence: attested to the start year by both encyclopedias; the end is contradictory, English Wikipedia dating the employment 1933-1937 and Portuguese Wikipedia 1933-1936, and the conflict is left open. The depot's street address is unconfirmed and the coordinate is the Botafogo district associated with the company's Rio works.
stops.campa: The Light and Power company hires him to wash streetcars and mend tires. Rio moves on rails the company owns, and he stands at the end of the line with a hose, sending the cars back out clean into a city that never watches him do it. Four years, or three: the two encyclopedias that carry his life cannot agree when the job ends. It is the last stretch of ordinary wage labor in his record, and every account gives it a single line, as though the years were a formality between the Navy and the crisis.
suggested_refs: Employment records of the Rio de Janeiro Tramway, Light and Power Company, unlocated

stops.name: Light e Power depot, the foot broken
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by Portuguese Wikipedia; no treating hospital, medical file, or compensation record was located in this pass
stops.campa: A workplace accident breaks his foot. Two surgeries follow, and a limp that stays with him for the remaining fifty-three years. Of all the physical facts of the man this is the one that outlasts the paperwork: visitors to the asylum decades later describe the gait before they describe the face. The injury also puts him in a courtroom, and the courtroom puts him in front of a lawyer, and the lawyer will give him the address of the last house he lives in as a free man.
suggested_refs: The 1936 accident litigation file, which the museum biography says brought him to the lawyer Humberto Leone

stops.name: Botafogo, the lawyer's household
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year and the district; the street is not named in any source, and the employer appears as Humberto Leone in the museum biography and Humberto Magalhães Leoni in English Wikipedia. An earlier pass gave the name as Jose Maria Leone, which no source supports; that name is struck.
stops.campa: Dismissed by the Light company, he enters the household of the lawyer Humberto Leone in Botafogo as a domestic servant. Leone had litigated the accident; the injury that ended the depot work has produced the next employer. He serves in a district of hillside villas facing Guanabara Bay, in a country where the men who do this work are Black and the households that engage them do not write their names down. Claude Lévi-Strauss is in Brazil these same years, in São Paulo and the Mato Grosso, transcribing the sign systems of people the state does not read.
suggested_refs: The Leone household in Botafogo, street unrecorded in any accessible source

stops.name: Mosteiro de São Bento, the summons
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both encyclopedias; the content of the vision varies between retellings, seven blue angels in some, a bare commission in others, and the variation is recorded rather than adjudicated
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of December he goes first to his employer and then up to the Benedictine monastery above the harbor, into an interior of carved and gilded cedar, and declares himself Jesus Christ, sent by God to judge the living and the dead. Accounts differ on what he says he has seen. One telling gives him seven blue angels. Another gives a straight commission and nothing further. The monastery stands in every version. One man walks in, sailor and boxer and servant. A messenger walks out, carrying an errand that will take fifty years.
suggested_refs: The Mosteiro de São Bento, Rio de Janeiro, site of the December 1938 episode

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the police description
stops.date_confidence: attested: English Wikipedia gives 24 December for the arrest, Portuguese Wikipedia gives late December without a day; the street of the arrest is not recorded and the coordinate is central Rio
stops.campa: Two days after the monastery the police take him. The record they write is a string of categories closing on an absence: wandering, Black, beggar, indigent, carrying no document that says who he is. It is the earliest surviving document about him and it is an inventory, made by the state, of a man reduced to what can be seen from outside. He will spend the rest of his life making the counter-inventory, item by item, with a label stitched to each thing, so that nothing in creation goes before God undocumented.
stops.quote: wandering black beggar [indigent], bearing no documents
stops.quote_source: 1938 police record, quoted in Marlon Miguel, 'Representing the World, Weathering its End: Arthur Bispo do Rosário's Ecology of the Ship,' Cultural Inquiry 17 (ICI Berlin Press, 2020), note 529; also cited via Luciana Hidalgo, Arthur Bispo do Rosário: O senhor do labirinto (Rocco, 2011), p. 18
suggested_refs: The December 1938 police occurrence record, quoted at second hand and not consulted directly
sources: Luciana Hidalgo, O senhor do labirinto (Rocco, 2011), p. 18, cited by Miguel

stops.name: Praia Vermelha, the Hospício Pedro II
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by English Wikipedia, undated to the day by Portuguese Wikipedia; the coordinate is corrected to the building of the former Hospital Nacional de Alienados, now the UFRJ Praia Vermelha campus, about 500 m south of the value carried in an earlier pass
stops.campa: On Christmas Eve he is committed to the Hospício Pedro II at Praia Vermelha, the first official asylum in Brazil, under the granite of the Sugarloaf. A man announcing a divine commission is locked up on the eve of the feast that celebrates one. He is examined here and named: the state, having already written down what he looks like, now writes down what he is. He is held a matter of weeks. Every address he holds after this one is assigned to him by a doctor.
suggested_refs: The Hospício Pedro II / Hospital Nacional de Alienados building at Praia Vermelha, now the UFRJ campus

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the number
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month by both encyclopedias; the coordinate is corrected to Portuguese Wikipedia's 22 degrees 56 minutes 12 seconds south, 43 degrees 23 minutes 56 seconds west, in Curicica, about three kilometres west of the value carried across earlier passes
stops.campa: In January he is transferred west to the Colônia Juliano Moreira in the Jacarepaguá lowlands, diagnosed paranoid schizophrenic, and registered as patient 01662. The grounds were a sugar estate, the Engenho da Taquara, before the state expropriated them and opened a colony for male psychopaths in 1924; they are pavilions, farmland, and forest, a town for people the city has finished with. The number outlives every other name he answers to. No traveler in the atlas has ever stood on this ground.
suggested_refs: The Colônia Juliano Moreira patient register, entry 01662

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, O Cruzeiro comes with a camera
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of publication; the identification of the photographed inmate as Bispo is probable and not certain, Portuguese Wikipedia saying only that the caption possivelmente refers to him, and the article names nobody
stops.campa: The photographer Jean Manzon and the reporter David Nasser come inside the colony and publish its inmates in a national magazine under the headline Will the mad be happy? A caption Nasser writes puts words into the mouth of a man photographed with his cloth: I am the envoy of providence, I was born on a star. The article names no one. Whether the man is Bispo is probable and not certain, so the most quoted sentence of his life is a journalist's line, hung on a body, sold on newsstands in 1943 while Antonin Artaud is drawing at Rodez.
stops.quote: Temores celestiais assustam alguns. Manias do poder divino. "Eu sou o enviado da providência. Nasci numa estrela e venho salvar a humanidade". Este teceu o seu manto divino e prepara-se para a viagem às paragens da eternidade.
stops.quote_source: David Nasser (text), photography by Jean Manzon, 'Os loucos serão felizes?', O Cruzeiro, 27 November 1943, n. 5, p. 38, digitized in the Hemeroteca Digital Brasileira; caption printed under a photograph of an unnamed inmate whom Portuguese Wikipedia says possivelmente is Bispo do Rosário
suggested_refs: O Cruzeiro, 27 November 1943, n. 5, p. 38, in the Hemeroteca Digital Brasileira
sources: David Nasser and Jean Manzon, O Cruzeiro, 27 November 1943

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, out through the gate and back
stops.date_confidence: undated and partly unverified: the pattern of periods of outside domestic work is attested by Portuguese Wikipedia, the escapes and recaptures are secondary tradition only, and no individual departure or return between 1939 and 1961 is dated in any source reached. The year is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Across these decades he is not continuously behind a wall. He goes out to work in private houses in Rio and he comes back; secondary accounts add departures of his own making and recaptures. Not one of these movements carries a date in anything reachable. The half century is spoken of as unbroken confinement. It is not unbroken, and the record of the breaks is gone. What the institution wrote down was arrivals. Everything between two arrivals is a hole with a man moving through it.
suggested_refs: Colônia Juliano Moreira admission and discharge ledgers, 1939-1961, unconsulted
sources: Secondary retellings of asylum escapes, flagged unverified

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the blue thread
stops.date_confidence: undated: no document fixes when the practice begins, biographers place its onset broadly across the 1940s to 1960s, the museum biography puts the decisive production after 1964, and an earlier pass wrongly anchored it to 1939. The year here is a placeholder inside the stated range.
stops.campa: He unpicks discarded Navy uniforms thread by thread and embroiders with what he pulls out. Blue on sacking, blue on bedsheets, blue on mattress ticking: words, maps, saints, the names of cities, columns of counted things. The cloth of the service that expelled him becomes the medium of the commission that replaced it. No document says when this begins. The asylum keeps records of bodies and not of work, and the work is the one part of him it never thought to date.
suggested_refs: The Seção de Terapêutica Ocupacional of the Colônia Juliano Moreira, pavilion unidentified in accessible sources

stops.name: Clínica Pediátrica AMIU, the attic room
stops.date_confidence: attested to the years 1961-1964 by Portuguese Wikipedia; the clinic's street address was not located in this pass and the coordinate is central Rio, an approximation
stops.campa: For three years he lives in an attic at a municipal children's clinic, working there and making there. It is the last address of his that is not an asylum. In Paris that same year a thesis on the history of madness is defended, and Michel Foucault begins the argument that confinement is less a treatment than a sentence handed down by reason on what it will not hear. The argument is written in a library of other men's books. The case is asleep in an attic in Rio, stitching the names of things onto sheets.
suggested_refs: The Assistência Municipal de Infância e Adolescência clinic, Rio de Janeiro, address unlocated

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the permanent return
stops.date_confidence: attested by Portuguese Wikipedia and by the museum biography, which states that by 1964 he permanently remained at the Colônia; an earlier pass wrongly downgraded this to an inference from the end of the AMIU residence, and the downgrade is reversed
stops.campa: In 1964 he returns to the colony and does not leave it again. The museum's own account places the decisive turn just after: a punishment, then a vision, then twenty-five years of production that nobody supervises and nobody interrupts. Brazil in this year passes into military government. He is inside a perimeter regimes do not reach, where no one asks what he is making or why so much of it. The rest of the life is a work record. Something on the order of eight hundred objects survives it.
suggested_refs: The museum biography's account of the 1964 punishment and vision

segments.name: The Inventory of Everything That Exists

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the Manto da Apresentação
stops.date_confidence: undated: no source establishes a completion date, and the garment is understood as built and rebuilt across years of institutional time; the anchor year is a placeholder in the late institutional period
stops.campa: He makes a cape to wear on the day he presents himself to God. The outside is crowded with applied insignia and stitched cloth; the inside carries embroidered names in columns, the people he intends to bring with him. It is a garment made for one appointment, on a date he does not set, before a judge he does not doubt. It is now the most reproduced object in Brazilian outsider art and hangs in a room where visitors photograph it. The appointment has still not been kept.
suggested_refs: Manto da Apresentação, Museu Bispo do Rosário Arte Contemporânea Collection

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the raft
stops.date_confidence: undated: the work carries no date in the collection listing or in the scholarship reached here, and the anchor year is a placeholder. An earlier pass named the work Balsa and treated the inscription as spoken description; both errors are corrected, the work being Jangada and the words being written on the object.
stops.campa: He builds a raft out of the colony's leavings and writes on it what it is for. The words are not a caption somebody else supplied and not a remark made to a visitor; they belong to the object the way rigging belongs to a boat. A man who served nine years at sea and never had one ship named for him assembles a vessel from institutional waste and assigns it jurisdiction over the maritime departments of every state in the federation, and then, in the next word, over the universe.
stops.quote: [It] represents the maritime departments of all states. Universe. Raft.
stops.quote_source: Words inscribed on the work Jangada (Raft), Museu Bispo do Rosário Collection, transcribed in Marlon Miguel, 'Representing the World, Weathering its End,' Cultural Inquiry 17 (ICI Berlin Press, 2020), p. 266, Figure 7
suggested_refs: Jangada (Raft), Museu Bispo do Rosário Collection, reproduced as Figure 7 in Miguel's chapter

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the banner of words
stops.date_confidence: undated: the banner Eu preciso destas palavras. Escrita carries no date in the sources reached. An earlier pass rendered the embroidered line as 'in the chest carries water, is name' and located it in a figure caption at p. 276; the rendering and the page are corrected here to Miguel, pp. 271-272.
stops.campa: One banner is titled I need these words. Writing. Onto it he stitches Africa, tasks, afflicted, and a misspelling that is probably drowning, and a line that will not be straightened into sense. His scholar renders it and then hesitates in print over whether rendering it is right, since the disorder may be the work. The asylum exists to sort speech into the sane and the discardable. Here the speech comes back sorted by its own maker, in thread, and declines the other sorting.
stops.quote: In The Chest Carries Water Is the Word
stops.quote_source: Marlon Miguel's rendering of the embroidered inscription 'No Peito Traz Água É Nome' on the banner Eu preciso destas palavras. Escrita, Museu Bispo do Rosário Collection, in Cultural Inquiry 17 (ICI Berlin Press, 2020), pp. 271-272
suggested_refs: Eu preciso destas palavras. Escrita, Museu Bispo do Rosário Collection, Figure 2 in Miguel's chapter; Paulo Herkenhoff's reading of the same banner
sources: Paulo Herkenhoff, cited by Miguel on the same pages

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the order to pack
stops.date_confidence: undated: the statement is transcribed speech reproduced without a date in the source, and the anchor year is a placeholder in the late institutional period. The broken English is a close translation of the transcription and is left untouched.
stops.campa: Asked what he is doing, he answers in a syntax nobody has smoothed: the mission is to represent the existence of Earth, all of it, and then to box it, because the order is to pack. He calls himself a slave, a slave of the Lord, and means the word to describe a compulsion rather than to complain of one. The voices, he says elsewhere, tell him to do this way. In France that decade Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari publish Anti-Oedipus out of a clinic where patients run the newspaper. In Jacarepaguá the inventory is already half packed.
stops.quote: My mission is that, it is to achieve that, what I have to the following day is to represent the existence of Earth that is there, everything I did. [...] I will be preparing and packing [encaixotando, boxing] the things. Because the order is to pack.
stops.quote_source: Bispo do Rosário, quoted in Marlon Miguel, 'Representing the World, Weathering its End,' Cultural Inquiry 17 (ICI Berlin Press, 2020), note 532
suggested_refs: Miguel's notes 528 and 532, carrying the 'slave of the Lord' term and the packing statement
sources: Marlon Miguel, Cultural Inquiry 17 (2020), notes 528 and 532
Bruno Hoffman, 'Arthur Bispo do Rosário,' Almanaque Brasil, via English Wikipedia, for 'The voices tell me to do this way' (unverified wording)

stops.name: Museu de Arte Moderna, Margem da Vida
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by the museum biography, which describes this group exhibition as the only showing of his work held in his lifetime; no opening date was located
stops.campa: His work is shown in public for the first time, in a group exhibition at the Museu de Arte Moderna on the Aterro, forty-three years after the transfer to Jacarepaguá. He is alive, and he is not present. It is the only exhibition of his work held while he lives. Rio's art world walks around objects made for a court it does not recognize, by a man it has just heard of, who has been an hour's drive away the whole time and whose address the state has held on file since 1939.
suggested_refs: Margem da Vida, Museu de Arte Moderna do Rio de Janeiro, 1982, catalogue unconsulted

stops.name: Colônia Juliano Moreira, the critic at the gate
stops.date_confidence: traditional: the credit to Frederico Morais is widely repeated in museum and biographical literature, but the exact site and circumstances of a first viewing inside the Colônia are not specified in any source reached, and the month is a placeholder
stops.campa: The critic Frederico Morais comes to the colony and looks at what has been accumulating in a cell for decades. He calls it a total inventory of a certain stage of Brazilian society, which is a true description and not the one its maker would give: Bispo is not indexing Brazil, he is indexing creation, and Brazil is what creation put within reach of his hands. The word art arrives from outside, attaches itself, and alters nothing about the work, which goes on being made at the same rate for another seven years.
stops.quote: Total inventory of a certain stage of Brazilian society.
stops.quote_source: Frederico Morais on the assembled oeuvre, quoted in Marlon Miguel, 'Representing the World, Weathering its End,' Cultural Inquiry 17 (ICI Berlin Press, 2020), note 539
suggested_refs: Frederico Morais's writings on Bispo do Rosário, unconsulted in the original
sources: General art-historical consensus, flagged as such

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the prisoner of the passage
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by Portuguese Wikipedia; no release date, director, or place of first screening was located, and the coordinate is central Rio
stops.campa: A documentary is released under the title O Prisioneiro da Passagem, the prisoner of the passage, and the phrase fastens onto him. Passage is his own word before it is theirs: he embroiders his record of his passage on the earth, meaning the transit of a soul through a world it was sent to count. The film turns the passage into a sentence and the prisoner into a subject. Both readings sit in the title at once, and neither is corrected by the man, who is filmed and does not explain himself.
suggested_refs: O Prisioneiro da Passagem (1982), documentary, credits unlocated

stops.name: Hospital Manfredini, the fifth of July
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both encyclopedias; the cause of death is contradictory and unresolved, Portuguese Wikipedia giving bronchopneumonia at Hospital Manfredini and English Wikipedia a heart attack at the Colônia. The two name the same complex, Manfredini being a sixty-bed hospital inside the grounds, so the contradiction reduces to cause alone.
stops.campa: He dies inside the perimeter, in a sixty-bed hospital standing within the colony itself, fifty years and six months after the transfer. The two encyclopedias that carry his life disagree about what stops it, bronchopneumonia in one and a heart attack in the other, and they are not in fact disagreeing about the place: Manfredini is the colony's own hospital, converted long afterward into a family clinic bearing his name. The inventory is unfinished. Its own terms do not permit an ending.
suggested_refs: Hospital Manfredini, Colônia Juliano Moreira, since 2022 the Clínica da Família Arthur Bispo do Rosário

stops.name: Jacarepaguá, the grave that is not recorded
stops.date_confidence: gap: no source located gives the location or subsequent fate of his tomb; English and Portuguese Wikipedia, museubispodorosario.com, and several Brazilian press domains were searched, the last blocked or returning 404. The date here is the day after death and is not an attested burial date.
stops.campa: Where he is buried is written down nowhere this research could reach. Not in either encyclopedia, not on the site of the museum that holds eight hundred of his objects, not in the press that reprints his face every carnival. A man who spent twenty-five years making certain that every thing in creation would go before God with its name stitched to it lies at the end unlabelled. This entry names no cemetery. Inventing one would be the single act his practice forbids.
suggested_refs: Burial records of the Colônia Juliano Moreira complex, 1989, unlocated
sources: Gap: searched English and Portuguese Wikipedia, museubispodorosario.com, and Brazilian press domains without result

stops.name: Parque Lage, Registros de Minha Passagem na Terra
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by Portuguese Wikipedia; the exhibition is posthumous, opening in the year of his death, and no opening date was located. An earlier pass gave the title as 'pela Terra'; the correct form is 'na Terra'.
stops.campa: His first solo exhibition opens at the visual arts school in Parque Lage, under the title he had already embroidered on his own cloth: records of my passage on the earth. He is dead. The phrase travels further than the man ever did. In 2020 an American psychiatrist and novelist, Daniel Mason, gives a collection of stories the English of that same line, A Registry of My Passage Upon the Earth, and words stitched inside an asylum in Jacarepaguá arrive on a jacket in an American bookshop.
suggested_refs: Registros de Minha Passagem na Terra, Escola de Artes Visuais do Parque Lage, 1989
Daniel Mason, A Registry of My Passage Upon the Earth (Little, Brown and Company, 2020), a collection whose title quotes Bispo's embroidered phrase
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Arthur Bispo do Rosário' (the 'inspired by his life' framing is unconfirmed and tagged as reconstruction)

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the state registers the whole of it
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Portuguese Wikipedia
stops.campa: Five years after his death the Rio de Janeiro state heritage institute registers his body of work as cultural patrimony, not a selection of it, the whole. The state that arrested a wandering man carrying no documents in 1938 now issues documents covering every object he made while it held him. Nothing is chosen and nothing is discarded, which is the only acquisition policy his own method would have accepted. He had been cataloguing on that state's behalf for fifty years without a commission from it.
suggested_refs: INEPAC tombamento of 26 April 1994, Instituto Estadual do Patrimônio Cultural, Rio de Janeiro

stops.name: Giardini della Biennale, a date that will not settle
stops.date_confidence: contradictory: English Wikipedia states the work was first displayed at the Venice Biennale in 1995, Portuguese Wikipedia documents it at the Biennale of 2013 and does not mention 1995, and the Wikipedia page for the 46th Biennale does not mention him at all; neither date is confirmed here and the conflict is left open
stops.campa: The work crosses the Atlantic into the Giardini, where the world decides what counts. One encyclopedia says 1995 and the other says 2013, and the published record of the 1995 edition does not mention him anywhere. The moment his objects become international is therefore unfixed, in exactly the way his birth is unfixed, at the other end of a life that opens and closes in years nobody has settled. The objects themselves are certain: eight hundred of them, catalogued and dated by no one. Nearly every date fastened to them is negotiable.

stops.name: Taquara, the institution takes his name
stops.date_confidence: attested: the museum's own page dates the founding to 1982 as the Museu Nise da Silveira, the renaming to 2000, and the addition of Arte Contemporânea to 2002. The coordinate is the museum's postal address at Estrada Rodrigues Caldas 3400, a separate point within the same complex from the Colônia coordinate used elsewhere in this file, and the divergence is left standing rather than averaged.
stops.campa: The museum founded on these grounds in 1982 was named for Nise da Silveira, the psychiatrist who argued that what patients made was work and not symptom. In 2000 it is renamed for a patient. Contemporary art is added to the title two years after that. The collection holds the Manto da Apresentação, the Grande Veleiro, Moedas I, Eu Vim. The institution that received him as number 01662 now keeps his estate, and the address of his confinement has become the address of his authorship.

stops.date_confidence: undated: both encyclopedias record a statue at Japaratuba and neither gives a dedication date, and none was found in this pass. The year is set to the 2009 posthumous Order of Cultural Merit purely as a placeholder and carries no evidential weight for the statue itself.
stops.campa: In the town where he was born in a year nobody can agree on, a statue of him stands. No source gives the day it was raised. The country awards him the Order of Cultural Merit in 2009, a hundred years after the earlier of his two possible births. He left this place as a boy for a naval school and never came back to it alive. The passage he spent his life recording ends where it started, in bronze, above a plinth whose inscription no source consulted here has read.

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, the king who embroidered the world
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by Portuguese Wikipedia, which also records samba school tributes in 1997 and 1999; no parade date is given, and February is entered as the carnival month rather than as an attested day
stops.campa: Acadêmicos do Cubango carries him down the avenue as its enredo: O Rei que Bordou o Mundo, the king who embroidered the world. Thousands of people wear versions of his cloth for eighty minutes in front of judges. It is the second court he has been presented to, and this one returns its verdict in points. Augusto Boal, taken off a São Paulo street in 1971 by the other arm of the same state and kept out of the country for fifteen years, had spent his last decades a few kilometres from the colony teaching people to perform their own lives.
